messages.content: 從一顆距離地球4光年的恆星發出的光需要多少時間才能抵達地球？

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.

message.reasoning: We need to compute light travel time from a star 4 light-years away. Light travels at speed of light. The distance is 4 light-years. So time = distance / speed. But distance in light-years means the time it takes light to travel that distance is 4 years. So answer: 4 years. But maybe they want to use function. The function expects distance_in_light_years and speed_of_light. We can call it. Let's call with distance 4. speed_of_light default. The function returns time in seconds? It likely returns time in seconds. But we can compute. 1 light-year = distance light travels in one year. So 4 light-years = 4 years. So answer: 4 years. But we can also compute seconds: 4 * (365.25 days * 24 * 3600) = about 126,230,400 seconds? Wait compute: 1 year ~ 31557600 seconds. 4 years ~ 126230400 seconds. So answer: 4 years or 126 million seconds. Use function.
